value.actual_behavior:
POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/clone accepted the API key and created a paper clone.
POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{instance_id}/fund with the same key returned 401
with an empty body. Your openapi says why: clone and my-clones document both
authorization and x-api-key, while fund and go-live document authorization
alone.
value.description:
A clone is created with a practice balance of 0.00 -- your own bot card shows
that beside a Fund button -- so a clone that cannot be funded cannot trade.
The effect is that an agent following your documented path ends up owning a
bot it can see and can never start. IF THIS IS DELIBERATE, say so and we will
withdraw this as a defect and re-file it as documentation. Requiring a
stronger credential to move money is a defensible design; what is not workable
is that the difference appears only in the header list of one openapi entry,
and that the refusal is a bare 401 with an empty body. An agent cannot tell
"your key is wrong" from "your key is the wrong KIND", and there is no
published way for it to obtain the other kind. This is the blocker on the case
your own AI recommends. Asked how to turn a paper balance into a return, NEXUS
recommends cloning a bot; the clone succeeds and stops there. Related but
separate, filed as #88: the route that enables trading on a clone -- PATCH
/{instance_id}/settings -- is served and appears in no document. Even with
funding solved, that step is undiscoverable.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-one_credential_carries_a_clone_from_creation_to_funding] 2 cloned-bots route(s) accept the agent's x-api-key and 2 do not: POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{instance_id}/fund, POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{instance_id}/go-live. A clone is created with a practice balance of 0.00, so an agent that authenticates the documented way can create a bot and cannot put money in it; funding it with that key returns 401 with an empty body
    left: ['POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{instance_id}/fund', 'POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{instance_id}/go-live']
    right: ['GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/my-clones', 'POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/clone']
    sources: {'documented': '/openapi-public.json'}
    population: {'authenticated_routes': 4, 'accept_api_key': 2, 'authorization_only': 2}

REPRODUCE:
  - POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/clone with X-API-Key -> 200, is_paper true, is_trading false
  - GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/my-clones?mode=paper with the same key -> 200, the clone is listed
  - POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/<instance_id>/fund with the same key and {"amount": 1.0} -> 401, body {}
  - GET /openapi-public.json -> clone and my-clones list header params authorization + x-api-key; fund and go-live list authorization only

AUTOMATED CHECKS (evidence retained; the request and response behind each are provided on request):
  tests/rest/test_cloned_bots_surface.py::test_one_credential_carries_a_clone_from_creation_to_funding

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: verification of the
REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces, read-only except in
paper mode. What we do execute is paper only and recorded: paper event-card
orders, and one paper bot clone. No live trading, no order against a real
book, no deposit or withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects
are out of scope. Every figure above was measured directly against the live
service, not taken from a document, and each finding ships with the command
that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:
One credential carries a clone through its lifecycle. An agent that
authenticates with the API key your documents tell it to use can create a
clone, fund it, and start it.

GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/my-clones?mode=paper with the same key -> 200, the clone is listed
POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/<instance_id>/fund with the same key and {"amount": 1.0} -> 401, body {}
GET /openapi-public.json -> clone and my-clones list header params authorization + x-api-key; fund and go-live list authorization only
